title: Mientras tanto: dos historias que ocurren a la vez

sections.content: Mientras tanto (meanwhile) signals that a second story was unfolding at the same time as the one just described -- useful when a reading needs to track several simultaneous occupations and resistance movements across different countries without losing the thread. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Mientras tanto, en Nicaragua, la presencia de tropas estadounidenses casi continua generó una resistencia armada liderada por Augusto César Sandino.
items.english: Meanwhile, in Nicaragua, the almost continuous presence of American troops generated an armed resistance led by Augusto César Sandino.

items.spanish: Mientras estas ocupaciones directas se desarrollaban en el Caribe y Centroamérica, Estados Unidos completaba la construcción del Canal de Panamá.
items.english: While these direct occupations were unfolding in the Caribbean and Central America, the United States was completing construction of the Panama Canal.

items.spanish: Mientras tanto, la propia Panamá se había independizado de Colombia en 1903, con apoyo militar estadounidense decisivo.
items.english: Meanwhile, Panama itself had become independent from Colombia in 1903, with decisive American military support.

items.spanish: Este periodo demostró que la voluntad de intervenir directamente en la región no dependía de la existencia previa de una amenaza comunista.
items.english: This period showed that the will to intervene directly in the region didn't depend on the prior existence of a communist threat.

sections.content: Mientras (without tanto) directly precedes a clause with its own verb -- mientras estas ocupaciones se desarrollaban -- while mientras tanto stands alone as a sentence connector, usually right after a comma or at the start of a new sentence.
